item.title: Queries
item.content:encoded:
A few questions:

+ Open
- Close
  • The article indicates that those 'trapped' in 826 become background characters, yet the experiment logs indicate that they can actually alter the main storyline to quite a significant degree. This may need clarification.
  • The article describes how, when leaving the room 826 is found in from within the transformed room with the text placed between 826, the subject will find themselves at the exit of its containment room. What happens if multiple subjects are in the room and only one leaves with the book? A time restraint after leaving, perhaps?
  • It is also noted that 826 transports those entering its transformed containment room will be placed at a random temporal location; will this location always be close enough to the text that it can be retrieved before the end of the story?
  • For texts without a plot, will 826 generate different environments on repeated testing?
  • When entering a transformed containment chamber, if said chamber has multiple entrance points, will they each lead to different spacial and temporal destinations?
  • Does a room need to have a door, or will a doorway suffice as 'leaving the room'?
  • On that note, could you only partially enter 826, thereby partially entering a spacial/temporal location, leave, and then re-enter to find yourself in a different spacial/temporal location?
  • Could one subject enter the room through an entryway, and then, say, a few minutes later, another subject enter through the same entryway; would this bring them to the same spacial/temporal location as it first did (thus meaning no time passed for the first person before the second entered) or will it be completely different? Could the second subject enter into a temporal destination earlier than when subject one appeared in the story?
  • What happens if multiple texts are placed in 826?
  • Do characters notice the appearance of entering subjects, or are they retroactively written into the story, however much has already occurred?

I might actually write something on these ideas, but I think it's best if I get some feedback on how to go about it. Anyone else feel free to answer these questions as a new log, too.


Oh, and also, can we change 'When a subject places a book between 826,' to 'When a subject places a text between 826,'? We already have the DVD experiment log, this feels like a change that should have already been made.

item.title: Regarding your thoughts Paul Fitzgerald
item.content:encoded:
Here are my thoughts on your questions…
So, how about printed works that don't have a set narrative?
Most likely details would be made up.

+ show block
– hide block

Or in a language, the D doesn't know?
Proven in an earlier experiment, the DVD, that the way the information is stored does not matter.

What effect would a bookmark have?
Perhaps as an entrance point to the story

Or having the dragons face inward?
Probably nothing.

School textbooks of various levels?
Depends on the book
Choose your own adventure?
It probably would create a new path based on what the subject does.

"Teach yourself whatever programming language in 24 hours"? Could get pretty surreal. Would it conjure a world that reads like stereo instructions, or strap the poor D into a brainwashing chair for 24 hours and spit them back out with additional knowledge but trips PTSD when they tried to use it?
Yea it could go that way, or create a world which contains physical representations of code based on analogies used in the book.. For example "fence post error" could be a fence around an area and having an extra fencepost crammed in at an angle… Conversely, perhaps if there is no narrative, nothing happens. Actually on second thought, most likely nothing would happen.

A videogame strategy guide?
Probably send you into a version of the game
WW2 era cipher book?
Perhaps send you to a scenario where you would use it. but as per my prior assumption it probably would do nothing
Star trek TNG tech manual?
You want to wander around an empty Enterprise?

RPG rulebook?
A world generated from those rules? Or nothing.
Bus/subway/airline schedule?
?
An atlas/tour guide/The Appalachain Trail companion?
Pretty straightforward, you would see a mock version of the described place

Philosophy or new age spiritual book?
Depends on book
The necronomicon?
?
Cookbook? Hm. Long pork. Make that a vegan cookbook.
You could perhaps end up in a kitchen with a chef cooking stuff

Evil time. Cut a slit behind the shelf the book is on, and insert (or remove!) story altering pages into the book while the D is in there?
unknown, insufficient data to extrapolate.

Use a book written with disappearing ink?
the text is still there, just not visible. So nothing different would change. ( of course, you could have things happen but this is my logical deduction )

A book with a journal style padlock?
behaves normally as if it didn't have a padlock
Raise or lower part of the shelf so the ends don't line up quite right?
the effect does not activate


Please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Just to add to Zyn's comment - the idea of all experiment logs (as with everything else on the site) are to be entertaining to readers. To tell an entertaining story in the form of experiment logs involves a balancing act:

(a) too much experimental protocol (finding the basic rules for an anomaly) can become dull, because storytelling is often the art of the unexpected and a series of control tests to establish the precise parameters of an anomaly may not provide that story;

(b) too much "random-idea-XYZ" can be irritating to readers, either because random for random's sake isn't a particularly compelling story, or because it breaks immersion to read about a Foundation that proceeds so unscientifically as to be ludicrous.

item.title: (no title)

Depends on if it's an open collaboration log or not.

Experimental logs under the purview of the original author alone tend to be a combination of "what if" and "here's how it works", while collaborative logs have more "what ifs" since the entries aren't all written by the original author of the SCP the log pertains to.

item.title: Thoughts and ideas.
item.content:encoded:
I had a few thoughts regarding this SCP
If people are entrapped into a book, then it could be used as a way to ethically neutralize some otherwise indestructible SCPs.

Information is something that seems to be able to be removed from inside without secondary effects. ( evidence is the recordings of the world within ) I submit that a story written which contains a book which has the answers to an unsolved math problem or other such thing of knowledge, have a d-class search for it, read it or scan it, and return. Items seem to have temporary existence outside, as such in dire emergencies objects could be removed and used.

If a person is rewritten into a story, and we can provide the story, then as a possible way to return them to some level of usefulness or as a way to reprogram d-class into scientists is to present a story such that all characters are loyal scientists at the foundation.

If things occur to a person while they are within the story and those effects persist afterwards, then a possible useage is to use artifacts within the story to possitivly change a person or do other things such as change gender.

It could also used as a probably safe way to dispose of things, you just leave them inside the book.

Or as a way to do research, such as use of a super computer within a story or use as a time dilation machine ( the subject would enter the machine and live many days inside while research is being done on a laptop or something else.)

And few questions I've been pondering upon, how does the language it is written in effect it? I would guess that it would not due to the fact it is able to read a DVD. If this is the case, what about the geological record as a story?( Where a core sampling of rock is used. Each layer of sediment is a record and thus a story of what happened as it was formed.)
Also what about electronics? If a laptop was placed between for instance?
Also if the room has more than one entrance, what happens when you enter the room through those while it was active?

As another idea which could be incorporated, imply that the real world is actually a storybook.

This is my problem when I read an SCP… I extrapolate all sorts of stuff from it and my mind tries to exploit its effects… Sorry about that, I had wanted to only make a small comment/question. I guess it kind of ran on didn't it?

Subject: Agent ███████
Book: "The Things Dr. Bright Is Not Allowed To Do At The Foundation", Foundation document
Equipment: One (1) canteen filled with water, one (1) watch, one (1) 9mm semi-automatic with extra cartridges.
Results: Agent ███████ returned after twenty-four minutes, visibly shaken. Agent ███████ entered an area nearly identical to the Foundation, the main differences being centered around Doctor Bright. Agent explained that Doctor Bright in this universe was a much more exaggerated version of the real Doctor Bright, enacting over-the-top shenanigans on a near-constant basis. When pressured for more detail, Agent admitted he had been captured by Doctor Bright, who proceeded to tie him to a chair, then confiscate, drain and urinate in Agents canteen. Doctor Bright then grabbed Agents 9mm, point it at Agents head, screamed "TRIAL OF THE DRAGOOOOOOON!", and kicked Agent in the crotch. After Doctor Bright ran off to "make a clown milk milkshake", Agent was rescued by Foundation personnel, who only asked where Doctor Bright had wandered off to. Agent proceeded to search the floor for SCP-826, and was able to locate it in Dr. ███'s office after fleeing another encounter with Doctor Bright, who was carrying what appeared to be a dildo taped to a large exercise ball. Agent approved for on-site counselling, further testing of this document is suspended.

A few edits:

1) It would be important, especially with this SCP, to specify if the material is a book or a movie.
Many books with movie spin-offs run very differently, and since books have no pictures, theoretically it is possible for no two people to experience the same scenario twice, though the plot will still be the same. Change has been reverted.

2) The format was good, but you had a few minor syntax errors with the quote box. Fixed and added in after the reversion.
